body:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty: PROD_Latency_Surge fired for service=runtime-edge (priority: P3)
joanne: acked. seeing the alert, joining. any customer reports?
sam: I saw a brief spike in 95th p99 for text-gen routes ~22:03 UTC, looks like 15s window, then cleared. no errors reported from clients yet.
devon: logs show a short backlog on router-3: `router_queue_ms > 2000` for a few minutes. pushing flush to that node now.
joanne: thanks. devon can you paste the prod query you ran?
devon: sure:
```
# prometheus
sum(rate(runtime_request_duration_seconds_bucket{job=\"router\",handler=~\"/v1/generate.*\"}[1m])) by (le)
```

devon: output showed a spike at the >2s buckets starting 22:02:40 -> 22:04:10 then dropped.
sam: I triggered router drain on router-3 (safe-drain) and scaled runtime-pool-small by +2 to absorb backpressure.
joanne: incident-bot noted an auto-resolve at 22:05:12 (PagerDuty auto-resolve).
incident-bot: PagerDuty: PROD_Latency_Surge auto-resolved (was fired at 22:03:05).
sam: looks like PD auto-resolved once router drained, but I still see a couple of anomalous traces around 22:10. small tail.
devon: re-fire: PagerDuty fired again at 22:11:47. must be a flappy signal from the router queue metric threshold.
joanne: acked. moving to follow-up mode. repeating mitigation: re-applied drain on router-3, temporarily lowered batching max to reduce tail latency.
sam: lowering batch_size_max to 8 on runtime-pool-small (was 16). applied.
joanne: can we verify customer impact? any 429s or client-side errors?
devon: querying logs: `filter(status>=500 OR status==429) | count()` for 22:00-22:20 -> 3 429s total across multiple customers, all short lived. I can pull request ids if needed.
sam: pinging support to check any customer tickets. @support oncall? (not in thread).
joanne: ok. moving to root-cause hypothesis: router queue threshold sensitivity + short GC pause on router-3 (I saw a GC event around 22:02:55 in node logs).
devon: GC pause 120ms — shouldn't cause that much queuing by itself but could amplify if combined with a burst. also saw a scheduled cron job on analytics hitting router-3 at 22:01:50.
sam: interesting — cron job likely caused a short burst to router-3 leading to queueing. the metric threshold then flapped PD.
joanne: next actions: 1) tune alert to require sustained >2s for 3 consecutive mins before firing, 2) add client-side slowpath logs to help correlate in future, 3) follow-up postmortem if repeats.
devon: filed follow-up ticket: INF-4129 (tune alert + investigate analytics cron affinity). link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-4129
joanne: support confirmed no escalations from customers — impact low but real (couple of 429s).
sam: mark as resolved in thread once PD clears. I'll watch for another 15m.
incident-bot: PagerDuty: PROD_Latency_Surge acknowledged by joanne at 22:12:10.
joanne: leaving handoff note for next oncall (overnight): watch router_queue_ms on router-3, check cron job affinity, don't remediate unless >5% customer error or >5s sustained latency. add me if unsure. :thumbsup:
devon: added a temporary rule to run cron on analytics-2 instead of analytics-1 to reduce affinity to router-3.
sam: thanks. no further fires in the next 18 minutes, I'm going to close the mitigation window.
incident-bot: PagerDuty: PROD_Latency_Surge auto-resolved at 22:30:01 (no active incidents).
joanne: closing thread. low-severity flap, follow-up INF-4129 owns the alert tuning and cron affinity. good catch on the transient burst. :eyes:
